content.text:
Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (geometry-shutdown):
Map nodes n71-n89 geometry/config and shutdown subtrees. Full named declarations, numbered reads. Return partial JSON.

1	const std = @import("std");
     2	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
     3	const terminal_size = @import("../terminal/size.zig");
     4	
     5	const log = std.log.scoped(.renderer_size);
     6	
     7	/// Controls how extra whitespace around the terminal grid is distributed.
     8	pub const PaddingBalance = enum {
     9	    /// No balancing; padding is applied as specified explicitly.
    10	    false,
    11	    /// Balances padding but caps the top padding so the first row doesn't
    12	    /// drift too far from the top of the window. Excess vertical space is
    13	    /// shifted to the bottom.
    14	    true,
    15	    /// Distributes leftover space equally on all sides so the grid is
    16	    /// centered within the screen.
    17	    equal,
    18	};
    19	
    20	/// All relevant sizes for a rendered terminal. These are all the sizes that
    21	/// any functionality should need to know about the terminal in order to
    22	/// convert between any coordinate systems.
    23	///
    24	/// See the individual field type documentation for more information on each
    25	/// field. One important note is that any pixel values should already be scaled
    26	/// to the current DPI of the screen. If the DPI changes, the sizes should be
    27	/// recalculated and we expect this to be done by the caller.
    28	pub const Size = struct {
    29	    screen: ScreenSize,
    30	    cell: CellSize,
    31	    padding: Padding,
    32	
    33	    /// Return the grid size for this size. The grid size is calculated by
    34	    /// taking the screen size, removing padding, and dividing by the cell
    35	    /// dimensions.
    36	    pub fn grid(self: Size) GridSize {
    37	        return .init(self.screen.subPadding(self.padding), self.cell);
    38	    }
    39	
    40	    /// The size of the terminal. This is the same as the screen without
    41	    /// padding.
    42	    pub fn terminal(self: Size) ScreenSize {
    43	        return self.screen.subPadding(self.padding);
    44	    }
    45	
    46	    /// Set the padding to be balanced around the grid. The balanced
    47	    /// padding is calculated AFTER the explicit padding is taken
    48	    /// into account.
    49	    pub fn balancePadding(
    50	        self: *Size,
    51	        explicit: Padding,
    52	        mode: PaddingBalance,
    53	    ) void {
    54	        // This ensure grid() does the right thing
    55	        self.padding = explicit;
    56	
    57	        // Now we can calculate the balanced padding
    58	        self.padding = .balanced(
    59	            self.screen,
    60	            self.grid(),
    61	            self.cell,
    62	        );
    63	
    64	        switch (mode) {
    65	            .false => unreachable,
    66	            .equal => {},
    67	            .true => {
    68	                // Cap the top padding to avoid excessive space above the
    69	                // first row. The maximum is the balanced explicit horizontal
    70	                // padding plus half a cell width. Any excess is shifted to
    71	                // the bottom.
    72	                const max_top = (explicit.left + explicit.right + self.cell.width) / 2;
    73	                const vshift = self.padding.top -| max_top;
    74	                self.padding.top -= vshift;
    75	                self.padding.bottom += vshift;
    76	            },
    77	        }
    78	    }
    79	};
    80	
    81	/// A coordinate. This is defined as a tagged union to allow for different
    82	/// coordinate systems to be represented.
    83	///
    84	/// A coordinate is only valid within the context of a stable Size value.
    85	/// If any of the sizes in the Size struct change, the coordinate is no
    86	/// longer valid and must be recalculated. A conversion function is provided
    87	/// to migrate to a new Size (which may result in failure).
    88	///
    89	/// The coordinate systems are:
    90	///
    91	///   * surface: (0, 0) is the top-left of the surface (with padding). Negative
    92	///     values are allowed and are off the surface. Likewise, values greater
    93	///     than the surface size are off the surface. Units are pixels.
    94	///
    95	///   * terminal: (0, 0) is the top-left of the terminal grid. This is the
    96	///     same as the surface but with the padding removed. Negative values and
    97	///     values greater than the grid size are allowed and are off the terminal.
    98	///     Units are pixels.
    99	///

content.text:
Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (geometry-shutdown):
Map nodes n71-n89 geometry/config and shutdown subtrees. Full named declarations, numbered reads. Return partial JSON.
